title: POC weekly sync - SDK tool/function structured output app integration
summary: Weekly POC sync to review app integration progress: SDK usage for function/tool calls, structured JSON output for order summaries, and tuning for latency and cost. Discussed small SDK snippet updates, streaming behavior, VPC networking note, and agreed on next benchmarks and a demo for product team.
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-17 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/meetings/ff-20260617-orsync-8421/recording
Attendees: Jake Thompson (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Lena Kim (Redwood SE), Maria Lopez (Orion CTO), Ben Carter (Lead Engineer), Sofia Ruiz (PM), Alex Nguyen (DevOps)

[00:00] Jake: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We tried to start right at 2. I think most folks are here — Maria, can you hear us?
[00:07] Maria: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks Jake. Appreciate you fitting this in, smaller sync than last time but wanted to go over the integration notes.
[00:13] Jake: Cool. Quick agenda: Priya will run through the SDK changes we pushed, show the function-calling flow for the inventory and order tools, and then we'll review the structured output JSON schema you asked for. Then we'll talk about latency numbers and a couple of next steps. Sound good?
[00:25] Ben: Sounds good. We had one blocker last week with the streaming callback; hoping that's fixed.
[00:30] Priya: Yes, Ben, we saw the callback race — we pushed an SDK patch that delays the finalization hook until the session KV cache warms up. You should see fewer truncated streams. We also added an optional onResponseComplete callback.
[00:42] Sofia: Nice — we had a few cases where the order_summary JSON was missing fields. Is that the same issue?
[00:47] Priya: Likely related. If the model returned the structured output before the function call resolved, some fields were empty. The patch forces tool calls to complete and returns the populated JSON. There are still edge cases if the model hallucinates keys, we'll add schema validation.
[01:05] Lena: Quick clarification — in your integration you call two tools: inventory_check and create_order, right? The inventory one is a read-only tool that hits your internal product DB, and create_order is a write tool that posts to your order service?
[01:20] Ben: Correct. Inventory_check queries stock levels via our internal API behind the V-P-C. Create_order posts to our orders queue.
[01:26] Priya: Okay, so for the VPC connectivity we recommended using our Private deployment connector — the tunnel we set up last week should support both tools but please confirm the IP allowlist. Alex, did you get the connector token?
[01:36] Alex: I did, but I had to update a firewall rule. The initial outbound port was blocked; that caused the connector to fail intermittently. It's open now.
[01:43] Jake: Good. Let's walk through the SDK snippet — Priya?
[01:47] Priya: Sure. I'll paste the flow in chat after the call but briefly: you instantiate RedwoodClient with the apiKey and region; for tool calls we register a tool handler that does an HTTP call to inventory_check, we return a structured object, then model receives that result and populates the order_summary. Example pseudo: redwood.client.call({ model: 'redwood-2-small', input, tools: [inventory_check, create_order], structured_schema: order_schema, stream: true }) — that's the pattern.
[02:20] Ben: On the model side, are you recommending a specific model for low latency? We want sub-300ms token times for interactive checks.
[02:28] Priya: For Orion's workload, given short prompts and structured output, we usually suggest a mid-tier quantized model — Redwood-quant-8 — on Dedicated if you need consistent tails. Hosted can get you decent latency but tails vary.
[02:40] Maria: Cost is also a concern; we have budget constraints for the pilot.
[02:43] Jake: Totally — that's why the Optimize recommendations matter. We can point the pilot at a quantized hosted model and then switch to Dedicated if you need guaranteed throughput. We also suggested prefix caching for repeated SKUs to save token usage.
[02:58] Sofia: About structured output — we sent an order_schema.json last week. Can you confirm how strict the schema enforcement is? We need guaranteed fields: order_id, items[{sku, qty}], total_cents, shipping_address{line1, city, postal_code}, and a status enum.
[03:15] Priya: We support schema enforcement at the SDK layer — we do post-generation validation and return a validation field if missing keys. We can also configure auto-retry with the model or fallback to a deterministic transformer that fills missing fields, but that increases latency.
[03:33] Ben: Would that retry loop consume more tokens? I ask because it'll impact cost.
[03:38] Priya: Yes, retries mean more tokens. A common pattern is to do a lightweight validator client-side and only re-prompt the model with a focused instruction to fix missing keys; that reduces token delta.
[03:49] Lena: Also worth noting our structured output mode can emit compact JSON vs pretty-printed, which saves tokens.
[03:56] Alex: One ask from security — do you log the full tool payloads? Our compliance team wants to know what lives in Redwood logs.
[04:03] Jake: We capture audit logs and request/response traces in Redwood Console, but you control retention and can mask sensitive fields. For Private installs, logs can be routed to your SIEM and can be stored on-prem.
[04:15] Maria: We need SOC2 docs. Jake, can you share the security packet?
[04:19] Jake: Yes — I'll send the SOC2 + ISO docs and the connector design. I'll drop links in the CRM.
[04:25] Priya: Back to integration specifics — Ben, you had an issue with the streaming callback ordering and partial JSON earlier. Did the SDK patch fix the race in your dev env?
[04:35] Ben: We applied the patch yesterday. In dev it's better, but in staging we still saw a truncated field when the inventory_check took more than 800ms. The model closed the stream before create_order returned.
[04:46] Priya: Hmm. We can make the SDK await tool completion before finalizing the event, but that will hold session resources. Another option is to stream a placeholder and send a final event with the full structured JSON when the tool finishes. That keeps the UI responsive.
[05:00] Sofia: Placeholder then final event sounds ideal — UX wants immediate feedback.
[05:04] Jake: Agreed. We'll push a small SDK change: stream partial result then emit final structured payload. Priya will own the patch.
[05:12] Priya: Noted. I'll open the PR after the call.
[05:15] [06:20] Maria: Quick question on telemetry — can we tag requests with our client_session_id so we can correlate logs with our own traces?
[05:25] Priya: Yes, you can pass metadata headers via the client, e.g., X-Client-Session. Those show up in Console and in the audit logs for Private.
[05:32] Ben: For the create_order tool, is Redwood able to do idempotency keys? We need to prevent double orders from retries.
[05:39] Priya: You can return idempotency_token from the tool response or have the SDK attach one. We recommend the client generates a token and passes it to create_order as a param. We'll add an example in the snippet.
[05:50] Alex: About the VPC connector — we want mutual TLS on the connector side. Is that supported?
[05:56] Jake: Yes, mTLS is supported for Private connectors. For hosted connectors we use short-lived tokens, but with Private we can do cert-based auth. We'll share the deployment diagram.
[06:10] Sofia: Benchmarks — last run you gave us showed 220ms p50 and 640ms p95 for the hosted quant model; is that still accurate?
[06:20] Priya: That was with 8-token average replies. For your order_summary length, expect p50 around 260ms and p95 around 780ms on hosted. Dedicated on comparable hardware pushes p95 down to ~420-450ms. We also saw batching effects if you run multiple concurrent requests.
[06:38] Ben: Our workload will have spikes at checkout; we need autoscaling behavior to keep latency stable. Can Redwood autoscale the Dedicated pool fast enough?
[06:46] Jake: Dedicated supports instant burst capacity and configurable autoscaling. There's a warm-up time for GPUs to spin up but we can assign reserved RAM to keep warm instances. For strict SLOs you can buy higher commit levels.
[06:59] Maria: Good — we'll include that in the success criteria.
[07:03] Priya: On cost saving: use prefix caching for product descriptions and repeated SKUs. Also consider lower-precision quant for backend tasks.
[07:14] Ben: Any recommended instrumentation for debugging structured outputs?
[07:19] Lena: We recommend hooking the tracing IDs to Redwood Console, enabling sample payload capture, and using the post-generation validator we discussed. We'll share a small debugging page.
[07:31] Jake: Let's look at the logs you shared — Ben had uploaded a small sample of two failing traces. Ben, can you describe one?
[07:38] Ben: Yeah, trace id 20260610-01 — the model returned an items array with sku: "123-ABC" but qty was missing. The tool actually returned qty, so mismatch indicates the model didn't merge the tool result properly.
[07:52] Priya: That suggests the merge logic in your tool handler returns nested keys under results.inventory, while the schema expects items[] at top level. We'll add a mapping helper in the SDK to flatten common patterns.
[08:05] Sofia: Could the model be outputting plural names differently? Sometimes it returns "item" instead of "items."
[08:11] Priya: Yes — that's why we recommend using enumerated field names in the instruction and schema enforcement to avoid plurality mistakes. Also we can add a canonicalization post-processor.
[08:24] Alex: Ops question — in staging we saw increased token usage after enabling full debug logs. Is that expected?
[08:30] Jake: Yes — if you capture full request+response payloads, that shows up in Console and increases storage usage. But it doesn't affect per-token billing to Redwood; it's more storage/retention.
[08:41] Maria: Anything we should be doing to minimize cost while keeping fidelity for the pilot?
[08:46] Priya: Turn on compact JSON, enable prefix caching for SKU lookups, and set a lower temperature for deterministic outputs so fewer retries. Also sample-only full payload logging to reduce retention.
[08:59] Ben: When will you share the updated SDK snippet and the PR?
[09:03] Priya: I'll open the PR today and tag you, Ben. Expect a new snippet in the repo and I'll post it in the shared doc: https://redwood.example.com/poc/orion/sdk-snippets.md
[09:13] Jake: I'll also attach SOC2 and the connector diagram in the CRM record (CRM-ORION-3982).
[09:20] Maria: Great. One more thing — our legal team asked about data residency for logs. We're in the EU but staff in US — we need logs stored in EU only for pilot. Is that possible?
[09:31] Jake: For hosted, we can configure region-based retention; for strict control you'd use Private. For the pilot we can set retention to EU region and disable cross-region backups. I'll confirm specifics in the packet.
[09:44] Sofia: Ok. If we move to Dedicated later, will the same SDK calls work? We don't want to rework integration.
[09:51] Priya: Yes — same API surface. You can pin model versions and rollout policies without changing the client code. That's one of the design promises.
[10:00] Maria: Thanks. Let's recap next steps.
[10:04] Jake: I'll go first: send SOC2 + connector diagram + update CRM. Priya: open SDK PR, push snippet with placeholder/final event flow, add idempotency example, and include mapping helper for tool result flattening. Lena: share debugging page and validation helper. Ben/Sofia: run a short staging benchmark with the new SDK patch and share traces by Friday. Alex: confirm connector firewall and mTLS plan.
[10:26] Ben: We'll try to run the benchmark Friday morning and upload traces.
[10:29] Priya: One more micro-item — we noticed the KV cache TTL default is 30s; for your checkout flow with repeated SKUs we recommend 2 minutes. I'll add that to the snippet.
[10:39] Jake: Great — any other questions?
[10:41] Maria: No, this was productive. Thanks.
[10:44] Jake: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the items.
[10:47] [END OF TRANSCRIPT]
